title_card.title: A solar storm hit Earth in 1859.
title_card.subtitle: Auroras reached as far south as the Caribbean.

caption:
In 1859 a solar storm made telegraph wires spark and lit up auroras as far south as the Caribbean.

In 1859, the geomagnetic storm known as the Carrington Event struck Earth. The storm produced auroras so intensely bright that people in the Caribbean could read night newspapers under the red sky while telegraph operators reported electrical sparks jumping from their equipment.

Visuals created with AI.

What would happen if a solar storm of this power struck our modern power grid today?
